newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO warns Hamas against wrecking Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: PLO warns Hamas against wrecking Hebron deal.

text.p: A top PLO security official threatened on Wednesday to use severe measures against the Islamic Hamas group if it tried to wreck peace deals with Israel in Hebron and in other Palestinian-ruled areas.

Mohammad Dahlan, the chief of Preventive Security in the Gaza Strip, was reacting to statements made by Hamas officials in Beirut and Amman against the deal clinched early on Wednesday to extend Palestinian rule to the West Bank town of Hebron.
"Our response will be very severe against any Palestinian group that tries to break the law or wreck the path of peace or harm Palestinian interests," Dahlan told Reuters.

Hamas officials in Beirut and Amman issued statements warning the Palestinian Authority against cracking down on its members under what they said were pledges made by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to Israel as part of the Hebron deal.

"The Palestinian people -- especially in Hebron city -- and the Hamas movement reject this protocol which is an extension to the Oslo capitulation accords and we warn the Palestinian Authority against a crackdown and an arrest campaign against the group in self-rule areas, especially in Hebron," Ibrahim Ghosheh, Hamas spokesman in Amman, said in a statement.
The Palestinian Auhtority committed itself in the Hebron accord to "fighting terror and preventing violence".
The PLO dealt a blow to Hamas's infrastructure in self-ruled areas nearly a year ago in a crackdown prompted by a wave of Hamas suicide bombings which killed 59 people in Israel.
Hamas has spearheaded opposition to the PLO-Israeli peace deals, vowing to wreck the accords through jihad (holy war) against Israel. Hebron is a Hamas stronghold.

"The protocol has abandoned 5,000 Palestinian prisoners and has pledged to hand over former mujahideen (fighters) and fugitives to (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's government," Ghosheh said.

Hamas in Beirut said: "Hamas is committed to its political programme and holy struggle in the face of the Zionist and (Palestinian) authority's campaign which targets this strategic Palestinian agenda."
Dahlan said Hamas officials in Beirut and Amman had clearly not read the deal.

"These so-called Hamas officials are spreading lies about the Hebron deal and they are simply people who are practising their rejection hobbies and and we are surprised at their rapid rejection to ending occupation of Hebron," he said.
"In the protocol, we have refused to hand over Palestinians to Israel and very soon prisoners will be released, especially women prisoners," Dahlan said.
